content.content:
Tilts-The-Jug: "There is, if the hands are careful enough. The Chapter takes from those who can bear the loss. It takes no more than that. A hand that breaks what it touches is no use to us, so I must see how yours work. Keeps-What-Floats stands on the dock just west of this door. He took a necklace of polished blue jaspers from a Lookout of ours, one of the Chapter, while that Lookout slept. He keeps it in a locked strongbox under the eaves north-west of the house. Bring the necklace back, so that the Lookout has it again. Do Keeps-What-Floats no harm. If he is hurt, there is no pay and no place with us. Here are three lockpicks. There are three ways open. You can open his strongbox with the picks, or you can take his key, which he may give for good talk or sell for coin. Sits-By-The-Water drinks with him on the dock. Ask her about his habits, because I will not tell them."

content.text:
I ran out of commands partway through the second quest, so I stopped there. One objective was still open: sell the Kothringi Glass Beads to Dar-Zeel.

- **First quest:** S'Tabi sent me to Tilts-The-Jug of the Night-Reed Chapter. She had me get a stolen necklace back from Keeps-What-Floats without hurting him. My Speech was only 15, so I picked his strongbox lock instead of talking him into giving me the key. I returned the necklace and got 100 gold.
- **Second quest:** Bent-Spine, the Chapter's fence under Lilmoth, made me a Lookout and set me to empty a drowned merchant's lockbox. I opened it and took the three pledges. I sold the figurine to Neeta-Haj for 20 gold and the Neesak charm to Okan-Tei for 45. Each was only half the fair price, because my Speech was too low to haggle.
- **A mistake:** I picked "What will you give me for the figurine, as it is?" without knowing it would close the sale at once. I'd have liked a warning.
- **The ship:** Boarding the coast ship and waiting did nothing, so I travelled straight to the marker for Bent-Spine instead.

I gave my full take to the game, and I'd want to play on.
